title: Shell completions via clap_complete
description:
## Context
Generate shell completions for fish, bash, zsh, pwsh via clap_complete. Wired through a hidden __completions subcommand.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** grove __completions fish, **When** run, **Then** outputs a valid fish completion script to stdout (parseable by fish -c 'source -').
- **Given** the same for bash, zsh, pwsh, **When** run, **Then** outputs the corresponding valid completion script.
- **Given** completions for subcommands, **When** generated, **Then** they cover all subcommand-scoped flags (not just top-level).

## Files
- src/cli/completions.rs — hidden subcommand handler invoking clap_complete::generate.

## Test Requirements
- Integration: 4 tests asserting non-empty output and presence of subcommand names in each shells output.

## Dependencies

## Notes
02-cli-ux.md completions section. Install location is documented in README; not auto-installed.

title: tracing-subscriber wiring (-v, -vv, RUST_LOG)
description:
## Context
Structured logging via tracing. -v sets level to INFO, -vv to DEBUG; RUST_LOG env var overrides everything.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** default invocation, **When** grove runs, **Then** WARN and above are logged (no chatter).
- **Given** -v, **When** invoked, **Then** INFO and above appear.
- **Given** -vv, **When** invoked, **Then** DEBUG and above appear.
- **Given** RUST_LOG=grove::git=trace, **When** invoked, **Then** that module logs at TRACE regardless of -v.
- **Given** non-TTY stderr, **When** logging, **Then** no ANSI color codes are emitted to stderr.

## Files
- src/main.rs — install tracing-subscriber early.

## Test Requirements
- Unit: 2 tests via the test-log crate or manual capture.

## Dependencies

## Notes

title: Color polish, NO_COLOR, table width
description:
## Context

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** NO_COLOR=1, **When** any command runs, **Then** no ANSI color codes appear in any output (stdout or stderr).
- **Given** stdout is not a TTY, **When** running grove list, **Then** colors are disabled automatically (is-terminal check).
- **Given** terminal width 80 cols, **When** rendering a table, **Then** the table fits without wrapping unexpected columns (truncate or stack as needed).
- **Given** a frozen project in grove list, **When** rendered, **Then** the tag is shown in dim style.

## Files

## Test Requirements

title: Epic: Phase 3 — Worktree mutations
description:
Implement new, fork, adopt, rename, freeze, thaw, done with WorktreeManager trait (gix for inspection, shell-out for add/remove/move). Integration tests via GitFixture helper.

See: 00-master-plan.md (Phase 3), 03-git-internals.md

title: Shell backend for worktree add/remove/move
description:
## Context
gix does not yet support worktree add/remove/move natively. Shell out to `git worktree` for these three operations. Trait abstraction allows swap when gix lands native API (issue #2596).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a target path and branch, **When** ShellBackend::worktree_add runs, **Then** it invokes `git worktree add <path> <branch>` and returns Ok on exit 0.
- **Given** a worktree path, **When** worktree_remove runs, **Then** invokes `git worktree remove <path>` (or `--force` when force=true) and returns Ok on success.
- **Given** old + new path, **When** worktree_move runs, **Then** invokes `git worktree move <old> <new>`.
- **Given** stderr from git, **When** the subprocess fails, **Then** the error captures stderr and is returned as GroveError::GitCommandFailed{cmd, stderr}.
- **Given** WSL with /c/ paths, **When** invoking git, **Then** paths are passed as-is (git accepts both forms under WSL) — but the test verifies no double-conversion.

## Files
- src/git/shell_backend.rs — ShellBackend struct implementing WorktreeManager mutation methods.

## Test Requirements
- Integration: 4 tests (add, remove, remove --force, move) against tempdir repo.
- Error path: invoke against missing repo, assert structured error.

## Dependencies
- Depends on: grove-rez.1

## Notes
03-git-internals.md section 2. Use std::process::Command. Inherit env (so git credential helper works). Stream stderr into the error.

title: grove new command
description:
## Context
`grove new <tag> [--issue N] [--branch name] [--base ref] [--no-fetch]` creates a new worktree, branch, and registers the project.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `grove new lazy-vm --issue 9947`, **When** run inside the desktop repo context, **Then** a branch `DESKTOP-9947-lazy-vm` is created from `if/master`, a worktree is added at `<work_dir>/lazy-vm`, and the project is recorded in the registry.
- **Given** no --issue and no --branch, **When** run, **Then** branch name equals tag.
- **Given** --branch overrides --issue, **When** both passed, **Then** --branch wins (warn).
- **Given** --base 25.3, **When** passed, **Then** branch is created from `if/stable/25.3` (uses repos default_base prefix logic).
- **Given** --no-fetch, **When** passed, **Then** no `git fetch` is run before branch creation.
- **Given** tag already exists in registry, **When** run, **Then** error DuplicateTag with hint.

## Files
- src/cli/new.rs — handler.
- src/git/shell_backend.rs — branch_create_from helper (or use gix-ref via gix_backend).

## Test Requirements
- Integration: 5 tests covering each AC.

## Dependencies
- Depends on: grove-4i5.1, grove-ktk.4

## Notes
02-cli-ux.md new command section. Issue prefix comes from RepoEntry.issue_prefix (per-repo).

title: grove fork command
description:
## Context
`grove fork [source] <new_tag>` forks a new worktree from an existing projects branch. 1 or 2 positionals; one-arg form infers source from cwd.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** cwd inside project foo, **When** `grove fork bar` is run, **Then** source=foo, new tag=bar, new branch derived from foos branch.
- **Given** `grove fork foo bar`, **When** run, **Then** source=foo explicitly.
- **Given** 1 positional and cwd outside any project, **When** run, **Then** error with hint to pass source explicitly.
- **Given** 3+ positionals, **When** run, **Then** clap rejects with usage error.

## Files
- src/cli/fork.rs — handler with `args: Vec<String>` + length validation.

## Test Requirements
- Integration: 4 tests covering each AC.

## Dependencies
- Depends on: grove-4i5.1, grove-ktk.4

## Notes
02-cli-ux.md fork section. Clap derive cannot natively express "1 or 2 positionals"; accept `Vec<String>` and validate in handler. Issue/branch flags same as `new`.

title: grove adopt command
description:
## Context
`grove adopt <tag> <path> [--move] [--issue N] [--base ref]` imports an existing worktree into the registry. With --move, relocates the directory into the repos work_dir first.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** an existing worktree at /tmp/foo and `grove adopt foo /tmp/foo`, **When** run, **Then** the project is added to the registry pointing at /tmp/foo.
- **Given** --move, **When** run, **Then** the directory is moved to `<work_dir>/<tag>` first, then registered.
- **Given** path is not a git worktree, **When** run, **Then** error WorktreeInvalid.
- **Given** tag already exists, **When** run, **Then** error DuplicateTag.

## Files
- src/cli/adopt.rs — handler.

## Test Requirements
- Integration: 4 tests covering each AC.

## Dependencies
- Depends on: grove-4i5.1, grove-ktk.4

## Notes
Move uses fs::rename when same filesystem, falls back to copy+delete cross-fs. Verify worktree by checking `<path>/.git` exists and is a file (worktree marker).

title: grove rename command
description:
## Context
`grove rename <old> <new> [--no-move]` renames a project tag. By default also moves the directory; --no-move keeps the path unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** project foo at <work_dir>/foo, **When** `grove rename foo bar` is run, **Then** registry key changes to bar AND directory is moved to <work_dir>/bar AND `git worktree move` is invoked to keep gits worktree links correct.
- **Given** --no-move, **When** run, **Then** only the registry key changes; path stays.
- **Given** new tag already exists, **When** run, **Then** error DuplicateTag.

## Files
- src/cli/rename.rs — handler.

## Test Requirements
- Integration: 3 tests covering each AC.

## Dependencies
- Depends on: grove-4i5.1, grove-ktk.4

## Notes
Order of operations matters: `git worktree move` before fs rename so git records the move correctly.

Freeze toggles the `frozen` flag on a project. Frozen projects are excluded from `grove launch`.

- **Given** `grove thaw <tag>`, **When** run, **Then** registry entry has frozen=false.

title: grove done command with safety checks
description:
## Context
'grove done <tag> [--force] [--keep-local] [--keep-remote]' removes a worktree. Refuses when uncommitted or unpushed work exists unless overridden.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a clean fully-synced worktree, **When** the command runs, **Then** the worktree is removed via git worktree remove, the local branch is deleted, the remote tracking branch is deleted, and the project is removed from the registry.
- **Given** dirty work in the worktree, **When** run without the override flag, **Then** error with hint mentioning the override.
- **Given** unsynced commits, **When** run without the override flag, **Then** error with hint mentioning the override.
- **Given** --keep-local, **When** run, **Then** the local branch is not deleted.
- **Given** --keep-remote, **When** run, **Then** the remote tracking branch is not deleted.
- **Given** override flag set, **When** run, **Then** all safety checks are bypassed.

## Files
- src/cli/done.rs — handler.
- src/git/status.rs — extend Status with is_pushed flag (gix-only, no shell).

- **Given** --default, **When** passed, **Then** repos.json default_repo is set to the new id.
- **Given** --issue-prefix DEV, **When** passed, **Then** the repo entry has issue_prefix="DEV"; without it, no prefix is stored (issue feature disabled for the repo).

Multi-repo grove list: scan all registered repos in parallel, group by repo, render current-cwds repo first.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Given** cwd inside repo Bs work_dir, **When** `grove list` is run, **Then** repo B section appears first, then others alphabetically.
- **Given** --repo <id>, **When** passed, **Then** only that repos section is rendered (other repos not scanned).

title: Tag disambiguation + strsim hints

## Context
With multiple repos, the same tag can exist in two repos. Disambiguation via --repo, qualified `<repo>/<tag>` syntax, or interactive prompt suggestion.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Given** cwd inside repo X and tag foo exists in both X and Y, **When** `grove cd foo` is run, **Then** Xs foo wins (cwd-based disambiguation).
- **Given** `grove cd desktop/foo`, **When** run, **Then** the qualified form unambiguously selects foo in desktop.
- **Given** an unknown tag baz close to foo, **When** referenced, **Then** error includes "did you mean: foo?" via strsim::jaro_winkler with threshold 0.85.

## Files

title: Broken commands: repo remove/default, list --repo, adopt --move-dir, launch
description: Four commands are broken in 0.1.0, three verified at runtime against tempdir fixtures during the 10-lens review (2026-07-11): grove repo remove / repo default are silent no-ops; grove list --repo is parsed and discarded; grove adopt --move-dir corrupts git worktree metadata; real (non-dry-run) grove launch builds argv that cannot spawn the configured shell. These are user-facing correctness bugs, not polish. Full findings: session scratchpad review-findings.md items 1-4.

title: Wire up grove repo remove / repo default (currently silent no-ops)
description:
PROBLEM (verified at runtime, found by 4 review lenses): `grove repo remove <id>` and `grove repo default <id>` exit 0, print nothing, and change nothing. main.rs:240-253 run_repo() routes both to repo::run(), which calls run_remove()/run_default() — validation-only stubs whose bodies say '// Validation only; actual write requires config_dir from CLI layer.' The functional run_remove_with_config()/run_default_with_config() (src/cli/repo.rs:242-252, 290-300) are called ONLY from unit tests. main.rs:251 has the tell: `let _ = config_dir;`. The RepoNotEmpty/--force safety check is therefore also unreachable from the binary.

FIX: In main.rs run_repo(), load a mutable manifest and dispatch RepoSubcommand::Remove/Default to run_remove_with_config(&mut manifest, config_dir, &id, force) / run_default_with_config(&mut manifest, config_dir, &id). Print a confirmation only after successful save. Delete or privatize the validation-only stubs so this cannot regress silently.

FILES: src/main.rs, src/cli/repo.rs.

ACCEPTANCE:
- `grove repo remove <id>` deletes the entry from repos.json and prints what it did; `--force` required when the repo still has registered projects (RepoNotEmpty otherwise).
- `grove repo default <id>` persists default_repo in repos.json.
- Unit tests updated to go through the real dispatch path; add a test that the stubs are gone (compile-level).
- Note: full binary-level E2E coverage lands with the assert_cmd bead in the tests epic; here at minimum test the new run_repo dispatch wiring directly.

title: Honor grove list --repo filter (parsed and silently discarded)
description:
PROBLEM (verified at runtime, found by 4 review lenses): `grove list --repo <id>` shows ALL repos. Command::List declares its own --repo (src/cli/mod.rs:72-75) which shadows the global --repo (so the global's help text is also hidden on this subcommand), and dispatch() (src/main.rs:133-145) destructures it as `repo: _` and passes `repo: None` with a comment that is wrong on both counts ('global --repo already routed via discover()' — discover() only selects the RepoContext used for section ordering; list::run() iterates all of cx.global.repos when args.repo is None, src/cli/list.rs:423-427). Perf side-effect: every excluded repo still pays a full status scan.

FIX: Bind the value in dispatch (`Command::List { repo, .. } => ListArgs { repo: repo.or(cli.repo.clone()), .. }`) OR delete the subcommand-level flag and wire the global cli.repo through — pick one, document it. Additionally make list::run() return GroveError::RepoNotFound (with did-you-mean hint) for an unknown filter id instead of filter_map silently rendering nothing (src/cli/list.rs:437-447).

FILES: src/main.rs, src/cli/mod.rs, src/cli/list.rs.

ACCEPTANCE:
- `grove list --repo X --json` contains only repo X; `grove --repo X list` identical.
- Unknown id errors with exit != 0 and a near-match hint.
- Regression test at the list::run level asserting single-repo output and the unknown-id error.

title: adopt --move-dir: use git worktree move/repair; refuse main repo; symlink-safe
description:
PROBLEM (verified end-to-end): `grove adopt <tag> <path> --move-dir` relocates a linked worktree with plain fs::rename (cross-fs: copy_dir_all + remove_dir_all) and never runs `git worktree move`/`repair` (src/cli/adopt.rs:37-43, helper 83-112). git's back-pointer (.git/worktrees/<name>/gitdir) still references the OLD path: `git worktree list` shows the old path marked 'prunable', a subsequent `grove done <tag> --force` fails with `fatal: '<new path>' is not a working tree`, and a later `git worktree prune` destroys the worktree's admin state (index, branch association) while the moved directory still exists.

THREE MORE DEFECTS in the same code path:
1. is_worktree() accepts the MAIN repo (.git directory — comment says 'Both count as valid worktrees'), so --move-dir can relocate the main repository and break every linked worktree's back-pointer. Refuse this.
2. copy_dir_all dereferences file symlinks (entry.file_type() is_dir()==false for a symlink, so fs::copy copies the TARGET content — e.g. materializing ~/.ssh contents), then remove_dir_all deletes the source. Recreate symlinks instead; only delete source after a fully successful copy.
3. move_dir will merge into an EXISTING destination directory, silently overwriting files. Refuse an existing dest.

FIX: When the adopted path is a linked worktree of cx.resolved.main_repo, call ShellBackend::worktree_move (already implemented, currently unused here); otherwise run `git -C <main_repo> worktree repair <dest>` after the filesystem move. Add the three guards above.

FILES: src/cli/adopt.rs (src/git/shell_backend.rs only if worktree_move needs signature tweaks).

ACCEPTANCE:
- After adopt --move-dir, `git worktree list` shows the NEW path, nothing prunable, and `grove done <tag> --force` succeeds — pin exactly the verified failure sequence as an integration test.
- adopt --move-dir on the main working tree errors clearly.
- Symlink-containing worktree survives a cross-filesystem move with links intact (test with a tempdir symlink).
- Existing destination dir → error, source untouched.

title: Fix launch argv: shell command must be spawnable; default to $SHELL
description:
PROBLEM (2 lenses; explicit divergence from spec docs/04-launch-test-ci.md §2.2/2.3): the real (non-dry-run) launch path pushes the ENTIRE shell command as ONE argv element and omits the `wsl.exe -e` wrapper. src/launch/wezterm.rs:45-48: `argv.push("--"); argv.push(cmd.clone())` — `wezterm cli spawn -- <arg>` execs argv directly with no shell parsing, so it looks for a program literally named `fish -l -c 'claude ...; exec fish'`. windows_terminal.rs:45-47 similarly passes the WSL-only command as a single Windows commandline token (wt happens to re-parse its tail, but the spec'd `-w 0 -p Ubuntu` window/profile flags are missing). Also: DEFAULT_SHELL_COMMAND hardcodes fish (src/cli/launch.rs:11-13) — on machines without fish every tab dies instantly.

FIX:
1. Build proper argv in both backends: spec form `... -- wsl.exe -e <shell> <args...>` when driving Windows binaries from WSL; on native platforms exec the shell directly. Split the command into argv elements (or wrap as [<shell>, "-l", "-c", cmd]).
2. Default shell from $SHELL when launch.shell_command is unset; keep the fish+claude command as a documented config example, not a baked-in default.
3. Add the wt `-w 0` / profile flags (or config knobs) per docs/04.

FILES: src/launch/wezterm.rs, src/launch/windows_terminal.rs, src/cli/launch.rs.

ACCEPTANCE:
- MockTerminal/build_argv unit tests assert the exact spec'd argv shape for both backends (single tab and multi-tab).
- Snapshot tests for --dry-run output updated.
- Manual verification on the WSL1+wezterm and WSL1+wt setups noted in the bead comments before close.

title: CLI UX: help text, JSON contracts, inference consistency, error quality
description: grove is driven by a human and by AI agents; both depend on --help and stable machine output. Review found: nearly every flag has blank help; fork shows [POSITIONALS]...; multi-tag status --json emits unparseable concatenated documents; --no-status only works with --json; freeze/thaw demand a TAG though the implementation supports cwd inference (done infers, freeze errors — inconsistent); unknown-tag errors use wrong variants ('repo X not found in repos.json' for a tag typo); error chains are truncated to the outermost message.

title: Help text for every flag/arg; fix fork [POSITIONALS]; visible completions
description:
PROBLEM (3 lenses): almost no argument or flag has help text — `grove new --help` shows <TAG>, --issue, --branch, --base, --no-fetch with BLANK descriptions; same for done's --force/--keep-local/--keep-remote, list's --short/--json/--no-status, status, adopt, rename, launch, repo add --id (src/cli/mod.rs:50-181). README explicitly defers to `grove <cmd> --help` for the full flag reference, so the promised reference is empty. Agents drive this tool from --help and fly blind (does done --force also delete the remote branch? unanswerable without source). ALSO: fork renders as `Usage: grove fork [OPTIONS] [POSITIONALS]...` — internal name leaked, arity unconstrained, zero-arg call fails at RUNTIME with the mangled `invalid tag '': fork takes 1 or 2 arguments, got 0` (fork.rs:106-109). ALSO: shell-completion generation is hidden (`#[command(hide = true, name = "__completions")]`) — undiscoverable, and clap's typo suggester won't offer it.

FIX:
1. Doc comments on EVERY field in the clap derive structs (clap turns them into help). Be behaviorally precise: e.g. --force: 'Skip the dirty/unpushed safety checks and delete even if unmerged'; --base: 'Base ref for the new branch (default: <upstream>/<default_base>)'.
2. Fork: #[arg(value_names = ["SOURCE", "NEW_TAG"], num_args = 1..=2)] with help explaining the one-arg cwd-inferred form; clap now enforces arity (usage + exit 2).
3. Expose a visible `completions <SHELL>` subcommand; keep __completions as hidden alias for existing wrapper scripts.

FILES: src/cli/mod.rs (+ small fork.rs cleanup for the dead arity error).

ACCEPTANCE: `grove <every-subcommand> --help` has a non-empty description for every option (assert in a test iterating the clap command tree: Command::get_arguments, help present); `grove fork` with 0 args exits 2 with usage; `grove completions fish` works and is listed in --help.

title: status: infer tag from cwd; emit valid JSON for multiple tags
description:
PROBLEM (2 findings):
1. `grove status` with no args fails at runtime ('grove status requires at least one tag', exit 1, src/main.rs:229-232) — no cwd inference, unlike done/freeze/fork. Run inside a worktree, the natural `grove status` errors instead of showing that worktree.
2. `grove status tag1 tag2 --json` prints N concatenated pretty-printed JSON documents (one per loop iteration, main.rs:229-238) — unparseable as a single input by any standard JSON parser.

FIX:
1. No tags given → infer from cwd via the shared project_for_cwd helper (see the quality epic's consolidation bead — use it, don't add a 7th copy); keep an actionable error when cwd is outside any worktree.
2. --json with N tags → one document: {"version":1,"projects":[...]} (array even for N=1 keeps the schema uniform; document this). Human mode unchanged.

FILES: src/main.rs, src/cli/status.rs.

ACCEPTANCE: inside-worktree `grove status` shows that project; `grove status a b --json | jq .` parses; single-tag --json also parses under the new envelope; snapshot tests updated.

title: Honor list --no-status in table and --short modes
description:
PROBLEM: `grove list --no-status` is silently ignored outside --json: src/cli/list.rs:434 `let want_status = !args.json || !args.no_status;` is true whenever --json is absent (the comment even admits 'table mode always scans'). A fast listing on slow WSL1 filesystems — the design docs' recommended script fast-path — is impossible without JSON.

FIX: want_status = !args.no_status, all modes. The table already renders status None as '?'; make --short do the equivalent. Document the flag (help text bead covers the string).

FILES: src/cli/list.rs.

ACCEPTANCE: `grove list --no-status` performs zero git opens (assert via fixture timing or a scan-count hook) and renders '?' status cells; --json --no-status behavior unchanged.

title: freeze/thaw: make TAG optional (cwd inference exists but is unreachable)
description:
PROBLEM: freeze/thaw REQUIRE a tag at the clap level (src/cli/mod.rs:111-113 `Freeze { tag: String }`) even though the implementation fully supports cwd inference — FreezeArgs.tag is Option<String> with a resolve_tag fallback (freeze.rs:19-42), and main.rs:186-194 wraps the mandatory arg in Some(). Dead capability + inconsistency: inside a worktree `grove done` works but `grove freeze` errors.

FIX: Freeze { tag: Option<String> } / Thaw { tag: Option<String> }, pass through unchanged. Help text notes the inference.

FILES: src/cli/mod.rs, src/main.rs.

ACCEPTANCE: inside a worktree, `grove freeze` freezes that project; outside, actionable error; existing freeze tests pass.

title: UnknownTag + shared did-you-mean everywhere (fork/rename/done use wrong variants)
description:
PROBLEM (3 lenses): unknown-tag errors use factually wrong variants: fork.rs:31-37 and rename.rs:16-22 return GroveError::RepoNotFound → 'repo '<tag>' not found in repos.json' for a mistyped PROJECT TAG; done.rs:50-54 returns WorktreeNotFound(PathBuf::from(&tag)) → renders a tag as a path. Meanwhile path/status/freeze correctly say 'unknown tag — did you mean ...'. The jaro-winkler suggestion helper is implemented FIVE times with drifting thresholds (path.rs:11, freeze.rs:10, status.rs:75, repo.rs:333, repo/mod.rs:195 — >0.8 vs >=0.8 vs >=0.85).

FIX: one pub(crate) fn suggest<'a>(input, candidates) -> Option<String> (single threshold constant; total_cmp instead of partial_cmp().unwrap()); GroveError::UnknownTag { tag, hint } (already defined, error.rs:43) used in fork, rename, done, and the existing five sites. Delete the five copies.

FILES: src/cli/fork.rs, src/cli/rename.rs, src/cli/done.rs, src/cli/path.rs, src/cli/freeze.rs, src/cli/status.rs, src/cli/repo.rs, src/repo/mod.rs (mostly deletions; helper lands in repo/ or a util module). NOTE >3 files — this is a mechanical single-concern sweep; keep the diff to the helper + call-site swaps only.

ACCEPTANCE: `grove fork nosuchtag x`, `grove rename nosuchtag y`, `grove done nosuchtag` all print unknown tag + near-match hint; grep finds one jaro_winkler call site.

title: launch: --terminal flag; error on unrecognized configured terminal
description:
PROBLEM: terminal selection is not controllable from the CLI and misconfiguration is silent: LaunchArgs.terminal exists but main.rs:205 hardcodes `terminal: None` and cli/mod.rs defines no --terminal flag (master plan Phase 5 specs one); an unrecognized terminal string from launch config (e.g. 'weztem' typo) hits the `_ => None` arm (launch.rs:157-160) and silently falls back to autodetect.

FIX: add --terminal as a clap ValueEnum (wt | wezterm) wired through dispatch; make resolve_terminal_kind ERROR on unrecognized configured values ('unknown terminal 'weztem'; expected wt or wezterm').

FILES: src/cli/mod.rs, src/main.rs, src/cli/launch.rs.

ACCEPTANCE: `grove launch --terminal wezterm --dry-run` selects wezterm; config with a typo'd terminal errors with the message; ValueEnum gives clap-level validation + completion for free.

title: Output consistency: converge JSON schemas, NO_COLOR in tables, repo show --json
description:
Three MEDIUM/LOW output-contract findings, one bead:
1. status --json and list --json describe git status with DIFFERENT shapes: status puts dirty/ahead/behind at top level (+dirty_files, head_branch, upstream); list nests status{dirty,ahead,behind,untracked}. untracked exists only in list, dirty_files only in status; the branch field is head_branch in one, branch in the other. Converge on one status sub-object (dirty, ahead, behind, untracked) embedded by both; status adds its detail fields alongside. Bump version field if shape changes (the versioning convention exists for exactly this).
2. Color gating is split: tag/branch cells honor display::use_color() (TTY+NO_COLOR+TERM=dumb) but status/issue cells use comfy-table .fg() unconditionally (list.rs:194-227) — NO_COLOR=1 on a TTY renders a half-colored table. Gate every .fg() on use_color().
3. `grove repo show <id>` has no --json while every sibling has one; add it with field names matching repo list's schema (+projects count).

FILES: src/cli/status.rs, src/cli/list.rs, src/cli/repo.rs.

ACCEPTANCE: one documented status JSON shape consumed from both commands (test deserializes both with one serde struct); NO_COLOR=1 table snapshot has zero ANSI escapes; repo show --json round-trips.

title: Error reporting: print anyhow chains; keep gix causes; fix adopt path message
description:
Three related error-quality findings:
1. main.rs:53-56 prints `grove: {e}` — anyhow Display shows only the outermost message, dropping the source chain (a serde parse failure in repos.json surfaces as a bare 'Registry error'). Use `{e:#}` (single-line chain).
2. gix open failures are flattened: gix_backend.rs:56-58 (and :24-26) map EVERY open error to WorktreeNotFound via map_err(|_| ...) — corrupt repo, permission error, lock contention all print 'worktree not found: <path>'. Add a source-preserving variant (GixOpen { path, #[source] err }) so -v shows the cause.
3. adopt with a nonexistent path reports 'path is not a git worktree' (canonicalize failure mapped to WorktreeInvalid, adopt.rs:18-27) — misdirects from a typo. Distinguish io NotFound → 'path does not exist: <path>'.

FILES: src/main.rs, src/git/gix_backend.rs, src/error.rs, src/cli/adopt.rs.

ACCEPTANCE: corrupt-repo fixture error mentions the underlying cause; adopt of a missing path says it does not exist; a nested error prints its chain.

title: Data safety: done deletion policy, registry integrity, migration
description: grove's worst failure mode is deleting uncommitted/unpushed work or corrupting its registry. Review found: done's safety check inspects the wrong branch and then destroys the very refs that made commits 'safe'; untracked files are invisible to both display and safety gates (gix is_dirty excludes them); repo add wipes existing registries; concurrent invocations lose registry writes; auto-migration fabricates author-specific config on other users' machines. Children fix each path and pin them with tests.

title: Untracked files must count as dirty (status compute, list display, done gate)
description:
PROBLEM (verified; 3 lenses): gix 0.83 Repository::is_dirty() explicitly excludes untracked files (gix status/mod.rs:193 sets dirwalk_options=None). grove compute() (src/git/status.rs:176-192) sets dirty = is_dirty(), computes `untracked` separately, and NOTHING consults it:
- `grove list` renders an untracked-only worktree as '✓ clean' green (verified: fixture with one untracked file → JSON dirty:false, untracked:1, table '✓ clean').
- `grove done` safety gate (src/cli/done.rs:61-88) checks only status.dirty, so a pushed branch with untracked files sails past UncommittedChanges; the files are saved only by git worktree remove itself refusing, surfaced as a raw GitCommandFailed dump. The test comment at done.rs:543 ('Untracked file → would block a non-forced done') documents intended behavior the check does not implement.
- Inconsistent with `grove status <tag>`, whose compute_detail treats untracked as dirty (total>0 || is_dirty).

ALSO: a branch with NO upstream (ahead/behind None) renders '✓ clean' via unwrap_or(0) + the `_ => "clean"` catch-all — indistinguishable from fully pushed. Give it a distinct glyph/wording (e.g. '– no upstream').

FIX: In compute(), derive dirty = is_dirty()? || untracked > 0 (fixes list AND done in one place). Update list renderers (status_cell/status_glyph/format_status/build_summary, src/cli/list.rs:194-243,347-361) to show untracked distinctly if desired (e.g. '+N?'), and give no-upstream its own presentation.

FILES: src/git/status.rs, src/cli/list.rs.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Untracked-only fixture: list shows not-clean; done WITHOUT --force errors with UncommittedChanges naming the tag; done --force still works.
- No-upstream fixture renders distinctly from clean in table, --short, and JSON (document the JSON field semantics).
- Snapshot tests updated deliberately (review diffs — these encode the fix).

title: done: safety-check project.branch tip, not worktree HEAD; guard branch mismatch
description:
PROBLEM: `grove done` decides safety from the worktree's CURRENT HEAD (src/cli/done.rs:78-94: status.is_pushed || commit_on_any_remote(wt.head())), then force-deletes project.branch with `git branch -D` (shell_backend.rs:63-65). If HEAD is detached or the user switched branches inside the worktree, project.branch may hold unpushed commits that were never inspected — and -D bypasses git's own merged check. Compounding: adopt.rs:45 falls back to branch=tag when HEAD cannot be parsed, so done can -D an unrelated branch that merely shares the tag's name.

FIX:
1. Resolve project.branch's tip via rev-parse refs/heads/<branch> and run the reachability check against THAT commit (not the worktree HEAD).
2. If the worktree's checked-out branch differs from project.branch, refuse to delete the branch unless --force, and say why.
3. Prefer `git branch -d` (git verifies merged-ness) and surface its refusal with a hint to re-run with --force, instead of unconditional -D.

FILES: src/cli/done.rs, src/git/shell_backend.rs.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Fixture: worktree switched to branch X while project.branch=Y with unpushed commits → done refuses, names Y, suggests --force.
- Fixture: detached HEAD → done refuses non-forced.
- Existing done tests still pass; new tests assert the refusal messages.

title: done: never delete the only refs that make commits reachable (remote deletion policy)
description:
PROBLEM: A pushed-but-unmerged branch passes done's safety check — is_pushed means ahead==0 vs the upstream, and commit_on_any_remote can be satisfied by refs/remotes/<fork>/<branch> itself. Then the DEFAULT behavior deletes BOTH the local branch (branch -D) AND that same remote branch (push <fork> --delete <branch>) (src/cli/done.rs:78-100). The only refs that made the commits 'safe' are destroyed in the same operation; the commits survive only in reflog. Nothing ever verifies the branch was merged into its base.

FIX: When --keep-remote is NOT set, require the branch tip to be contained in a ref OTHER than <fork_remote>/<branch> (the base branch, or any other remote ref) before deleting the remote branch. If the fork ref is the only container, refuse with an actionable hint: 'branch X is pushed but not merged anywhere else; use --keep-remote to remove the worktree but keep the branch, or --force to delete anyway.'

FILES: src/cli/done.rs (reuse/extend commit_on_any_remote in src/git/shell_backend.rs to exclude a given ref).

ACCEPTANCE:
- Fixture: branch pushed to fork only, not merged → default done refuses; --keep-remote succeeds and `git ls-remote --heads <bare>` still lists the branch; --force deletes everything.
- Fixture: branch merged into base → default done removes local+remote as today.
- Strengthen the existing keep_remote test to actually assert remote-ref presence/absence (it currently only checks 'no error' — noted by the tests lens).

title: repo add: never overwrite an existing registry; dedupe by canonical path
description:
PROBLEM: `grove repo add` unconditionally writes an EMPTY registry to <path>/.grove/registry.json (src/cli/repo.rs:141-146: Registry::default().save(&grove_dir) with no existence check). Re-adding a previously managed repo — or adding the same path under a new id, since the duplicate check is on id, not path — wipes every project entry. Only one .bak generation survives and the next save clobbers it.

FIX:
1. Only write the empty registry when .grove/registry.json does not exist; if it exists, load it and print 'found existing registry with N projects'.
2. Reject adding a path that (canonicalized) is already registered under another id, with a message naming the existing id.

FILES: src/cli/repo.rs.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Re-running repo add on a repo with registered projects leaves registry.json byte-identical and reports the project count.
- Same path, different id → error naming the existing id.
- Tests for both, plus the fresh-repo case still creating the empty registry.

title: Registry: prevent lost updates from concurrent grove invocations
description:
PROBLEM (2 lenses): every mutating command clones the Registry loaded at process start, mutates the clone, and saves (e.g. done.rs:103-109, new.rs:61-67, freeze/fork/adopt likewise). registry save (src/registry/mod.rs:62-77) is tmp+rename — atomic against torn files but NOT against lost updates. Two concurrent grove processes (multiple terminal tabs, agent swarms — the tool's core audience) silently erase each other's registry entries: the worktree exists on disk but vanishes from the registry.

FIX: Take an exclusive lock around load-modify-save. Simplest robust shape: a lock file .grove/registry.lock held via fd-lock/fs2 (new small dep — check the ≤30-dep budget in AGENTS.md; std-only advisory lock via create_new + retry is acceptable fallback), and reload the registry from disk after acquiring the lock, apply the mutation to the FRESH copy, save, release. Consider a RepoContext::update_registry(closure) helper so all six call sites go through one code path (the quality lens wants this dedupe anyway — coordinate, don't duplicate).

FILES: src/registry/mod.rs (+ mutating call sites if the helper lands here).

ACCEPTANCE:
- Two-thread test: load registry with projects A+B; thread 1 removes A, thread 2 removes B, both save through the new path → final on-disk registry has neither (no lost update).
- Lock contention times out with a clear error rather than hanging forever.
- All existing registry round-trip tests pass unchanged.

title: Migration: abort partial-state branch instead of fabricating author-specific config
description:
PROBLEM (2 lenses): the partial-state migration branch (legacy registry.json present, config.json absent; src/migrate/mod.rs:225-244, 299-331) GUESSES the author's machine layout in production: work_dir '/c/work/desktop' (env overrides GROVE_MIGRATE_DEFAULT_* are test-only), derive_repo_id fallback 'desktop', remotes 'if'/'my', issue_prefix Some("DESKTOP") for every migrated repo. It then writes the migrated registry to the guessed path (overwriting any registry.json there, one .bak) and renames the legacy registry.json away — automatically, on first invocation, with no confirmation. Any external user hitting this branch gets the author's config fabricated onto their machine.

ALSO in migration: legacy freeze_expires is parsed then silently dropped (LegacyProject field never read after deserialization), and duplicate-tag insert errors are swallowed (`let _ = new_registry.insert(...)`).

FIX:
1. In the config.json-absent branch: abort with an actionable error ('legacy registry found at <path> but no config.json; run `grove repo add <path>` to register the repo, then re-run') instead of guessing. Remove the hardcoded defaults entirely.
2. When migrating with full config: print a per-project notice when freeze_expires is non-null (data being dropped), and log skipped duplicate tags instead of ignoring them.

FILES: src/migrate/mod.rs.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Fixture with registry-only legacy state → clean error, legacy files untouched (no rename, no write).
- Fixture with freeze_expires set → migration succeeds and prints the notice.
- Existing migrate tests updated; the GROVE_MIGRATE_DEFAULT_* env vars deleted along with the code they served.

title: Durable writes: fsync before rename; .bak rotation for repos.json
description:
PROBLEM: all three atomic writers (src/registry/mod.rs:73-75, src/config/global.rs:84-86, src/migrate/mod.rs:179-187) do fs::write(tmp) + fs::rename with no fsync of the temp file (or parent dir). On power loss the rename can be durable while the data is not — zero-length/truncated registry.json or repos.json. repos.json additionally has NO .bak rotation (registry.json has one generation).

FIX: One shared write_atomic(path, bytes) helper: File::create → write_all → sync_all → rename (+ best-effort parent-dir fsync on Unix). Use it in all three sites. Add the same .bak roll ReposManifest::save that Registry::save has.

FILES: src/registry/mod.rs, src/config/global.rs, src/migrate/mod.rs (helper can live in a small util module).

ACCEPTANCE: existing round-trip tests pass; new test asserts .bak created for repos.json on second save; all three call sites route through the one helper (grep-level check in review).

title: done: report deletion failures and print target before destructive removal
description:
PROBLEM: local and remote branch deletion errors are swallowed unconditionally (src/cli/done.rs:92-100: `let _ = backend.branch_delete(...)`, `let _ = backend.remote_branch_delete(...)`) followed by an unconditional 'Removed project' success print. The comments justify ignoring 'already gone', but auth/network/permission failures are hidden too — the user is told success while the remote branch still exists. Related (security lens): the tag/worktree targeted by done is inferred from GROVE_ORIG_CWD, and with --force nothing shows WHAT is about to be removed.

FIX:
1. Inspect deletion results: treat 'not found'/'remote ref does not exist' stderr as benign; print a warning (not silent, not fatal) for anything else.
2. Before removal, print the resolved tag + worktree path (always), so an inferred-tag mistake is visible; this also covers the security lens's GROVE_ORIG_CWD trust concern.

FILES: src/cli/done.rs.

ACCEPTANCE: fixture with unreachable remote → done completes but prints a warning naming the branch; output includes 'Removing <tag> (<path>)' line; tests assert both.

title: Docs & release: fix the install story before announcing 0.1.0
description: The README install section is entirely non-functional: the crates.io name 'grove' is owned by an unrelated 2021 segment-tree library, publish-jobs=[], there are zero GitHub releases and no release workflow despite the v0.1.0 tag. README documents a wrong config layout; cargo-dist is configured twice with conflicting values; AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/master-plan contain stale canon (crates not in tree, MSRV 1.80 vs actual 1.89, safeguards keyed to closed beads).

title: Fix the install story: crate name, release workflow, actual 0.1.0 artifacts
description:
PROBLEM (release blocker): README's install section is entirely non-functional. (1) `cargo binstall grove` / `cargo install grove` resolve to a DIFFERENT crate — crates.io 'grove' has been owned since 2021 by an unrelated segment-tree library (no binary); this project sets publish-jobs=[] and is unpublished. (2) README points at github releases for tarballs but there are ZERO releases and no release workflow (.github/workflows/ has only ci.yml) despite the v0.1.0 tag — pushing the tag triggered nothing. (3) cargo-dist is configured TWICE with conflicting values: Cargo.toml [workspace.metadata.dist] pins 0.28.0/4 targets, dist-workspace.toml pins 0.21.0/5 targets (adds aarch64-linux); modern dist reads dist-workspace.toml.

FIX:
1. DECISION (record in bead comments): publish to crates.io under an available name (grove-cli? grv?) with `[[bin]] name = "grove"`, or stay git/GitHub-releases-only. Update README install section to match reality either way; interim: `cargo install --git https://github.com/oysteinkrog/grove`.
2. Delete [workspace.metadata.dist] from Cargo.toml; single-source dist-workspace.toml; pick one cargo-dist version + target list.
3. `dist init`/`dist generate` → commit release.yml; re-run the v0.1.0 release (retag or 0.1.1) so artifacts actually exist; verify the release URL in README works.

FILES: README.md, Cargo.toml, dist-workspace.toml, .github/workflows/release.yml.

ACCEPTANCE: every install command in README executes successfully on a clean machine; `gh release list` shows artifacts for the current tag.

title: README accuracy: config layout, command list, flags, no-telemetry statement
description:
PROBLEM: README misdocuments shipped behavior:
1. Claims per-repo state lives at ~/.config/grove/<repo>/{registry,config}.json — actually only repos.json lives under ~/.config/grove/; per-repo registry/config live at <work_dir>/.grove/{registry.json,config.json} (repo/mod.rs:25-33; sandbox-verified). Users inspecting/backing up state look in the wrong place.
2. Intro lists 'move' among supported operations — no `grove move` exists (rename + adopt --move-dir cover it).
3. `grove list` row documents [--short | --json] only; --no-status is undocumented everywhere.
4. Master plan promises an explicit no-telemetry statement in README ('Telemetry: None, ever') — absent.

FIX: rewrite the Configuration section (global index vs per-repo .grove/), fix the intro verb list, document --no-status (and GROVE_CONFIG_DIR once that bead lands), add the telemetry line.

FILES: README.md.

ACCEPTANCE: every path, command, and flag named in README exists and behaves as stated (spot-check against --help output); telemetry statement present.

title: Refresh agent-facing docs: AGENTS.md canon, CLAUDE.md safeguards, master-plan status
description:
PROBLEM: the agent-facing docs mislead the agents that read them first:
1. AGENTS.md tech-stack canon lists crates NOT in the tree: color-eyre (main.rs uses eprintln!), dunce (absent — though the hardening epic adds it; coordinate), assert_cmd+predicates (absent — the tests epic adds them; coordinate). Agents told to follow canon will expect/add crates the codebase omits.
2. CLAUDE.md critical safeguards are keyed to CLOSED beads (grove-ktk.6, grove-1bt.4) — an agent cannot tell if the no-cargo-run-against-real-config rule still applies, and the 'legacy Python grove in production' claim is unverifiable; the cutover artifacts (published release) do not actually exist despite grove-1bt.4 being closed.
3. docs/00-master-plan.md: no done/pending markers though phases 0-6 are essentially complete; MSRV documented 1.80 vs Cargo.toml rust-version 1.89; 'source of truth' framing contradicted by shipped CLI.

FIX: update the canon table to match Cargo.toml as-landed (after the dunce/assert_cmd beads); rewrite CLAUDE.md safeguards for the post-0.1.0 state (explicitly: are real-config runs allowed? did the ~/bin/grove cutover happen?); add per-phase status markers + correct MSRV in the master plan.

FILES: AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, docs/00-master-plan.md.

ACCEPTANCE: no crate named in canon that is absent from Cargo.toml; no safeguard referencing a closed bead without stating current applicability; master plan states 0.1.0 status per phase.

title: Banner design docs 01-04 as pre-implementation; note shipped-surface divergences
description:
PROBLEM: docs/00 declares each detail doc 'the source of truth for its facet' and AGENTS.md points agents at docs/02 for the subcommand inventory, but the shipped CLI diverges on ~15 axes: no ls/mv/unfreeze aliases, no -i/-b short flags, no --tags-only/--all/--check-remote on list, no config subcommand group, no repo set, no freeze --lifetime/--timeout, launch keeps --only (not deprecated) and lacks --wezterm/--frozen/--no-continue, completions hidden as __completions, cd/path/rename/freeze tags required not cwd-inferred, cd prints a bare path not the __POSTCD__ sentinel docs/02 calls a mandatory stable protocol (grep POSTCD src/ → nothing).

FIX: add a banner to docs/01-04: 'Pre-implementation design (Phase N planning). The code and `grove --help` are authoritative; known divergences listed in <link or section>.' Adjust docs/00's source-of-truth sentence. Do NOT rewrite the docs to match code (history is useful); the divergence list doubles as a menu of candidate UX features (some — cd inference, cwd-optional tags — are already beads in this review).

FILES: docs/00-master-plan.md, docs/01-architecture.md, docs/02-cli-ux.md, docs/03-git-internals.md, docs/04-launch-test-ci.md.

ACCEPTANCE: every detail doc opens with the banner; docs/02 divergences enumerated once.

title: Feature backlog from review (agent-swarm & lifecycle features)
description: 14 feature proposals from the review's feature lens, ranked by impact/effort. Top cluster serves the owner's agent-swarm workflow (bulk worktree allocation, JSON on mutating commands, cross-worktree exec, prune, hooks, doctor). Each child bead carries the full proposal; implement opportunistically after EPIC_A/EPIC_B land.

title: grove alloc: bulk worktree allocation for agent swarms (JSON out)
description:
HIGH impact / S-M effort. Atomically create N worktrees in one call: `grove alloc 5 --prefix swarm [--base X] --json` → swarm-01..swarm-05, emitting a version:1 JSON array of {tag, path, branch} on stdout. THE missing primitive for the owner's agent-swarm workflow: a leader hands each teammate its own worktree without racing N separate `grove new` calls (see the registry-locking bead — alloc under one lock acquisition sidesteps the race entirely and is the cleanest consumer of that work).
WHY CHEAP: cli/new.rs already has the full create pipeline (fetch once, branch, worktree add, registry insert); alloc = loop + the JsonOutput{version:1} envelope pattern from list.rs. Fetch ONCE for the batch, not per tag.
ACCEPTANCE: `grove alloc 3 --prefix t --json | jq length` == 3; partial failure rolls back cleanly or reports per-tag status (decide + document); tags validate via validate_tag; single registry lock/save for the batch.

title: copy_on_create globs: carry untracked essentials into new worktrees
description:
MEDIUM impact / M effort. Per-repo `copy_on_create = [".env", ".envrc", ".claude/settings.local.json"]` glob list; on new/fork, matching untracked files copy from the main repo (or fork source) into the fresh worktree. Untracked-config loss is the sharpest recurring paper cut of worktree workflows.
WHY CHEAP: same PerRepoConfig extension point as lifecycle hooks; runs at the end of the existing new/fork pipeline. Simple manual walk keeps it dep-free (or a small glob crate — budget check).
RELATIONSHIP: hooks (post_create) can DO this via cp — copy_on_create is the declarative 90% case; implement after hooks and share the execution point.
ACCEPTANCE: globs copy on new and fork; missing sources are silent no-ops; never overwrites files git created; documented alongside hooks with a worked .env example.

title: grove sync: fetch once per repo, ff/rebase clean worktrees onto base
description:
MEDIUM impact / M effort. One fetch per repo (not per worktree), then parallel fast-forward (--rebase opt-in) of each CLEAN worktree onto its recorded base, skipping dirty/frozen/diverged with per-project reasons in a summary table. Keeps long-lived worktrees from drifting weeks behind main.
WHY CHEAP: Project records base; ShellBackend has fetch; gix has ahead/behind; rayon fan-out pattern exists; skip logic reuses done's dirty detection (post safety-fix semantics — untracked counts).
SAFETY: never touch dirty/diverged worktrees; rebase only with the explicit flag; --dry-run first-class.
ACCEPTANCE: behind-only clean worktree ffs; dirty/frozen skipped with reason; diverged skipped without --rebase; single fetch per repo asserted.

title: launch: single-target launch + dedupe already-open tabs
description:
MEDIUM impact / M effort. (1) `grove launch <tag>` opens ONE tab for one project (today launch is all-or-nothing via --only). (2) Dedupe: skip projects that already have a live tab/pane cwd'd at their worktree — wezterm exposes `wezterm cli list --format json`; wt.exe gets best-effort (likely none; document). Re-running launch today duplicates every tab.
WHY CHEAP: the Terminal trait + MockTerminal make 'query existing panes' a clean trait-method addition, testable without a real terminal; --only parsing already handles tag filtering.
TIMING: after the launch argv fix + platform-detection beads (same files, and no point deduping tabs that can't spawn).
ACCEPTANCE: MockTerminal test: second launch spawns only missing tabs; positional tag launches exactly one; --force-all overrides dedupe.

title: Per-project notes: grove note <tag> [text], shown in list/status
description:
LOW impact / S effort. `grove note <tag> [text]` stores a free-text note on the Project record (no arg prints it; --clear removes); shown in list (truncated column or on-demand) and status. Gives a 15-worktree registry the 'why does this exist' context branch names lose after a week.
WHY CHEAP: Project is serde with #[serde(default)] — note: Option<String> is a backward-compatible one-field change; registry round-trip tests already guard the schema.
ACCEPTANCE: note set/get/clear round-trips the registry; list renders truncated note without breaking table width (comfy-table handles it); JSON includes the full note.

title: grove prompt: shell prompt segment for the current worktree
description:
LOW impact / S effort. `grove prompt` prints a compact segment (repo:tag, optional dirty/ahead markers with --status) when cwd is inside a registered worktree; exits 0 silently otherwise — embeddable in fish/starship prompts. Makes 'which worktree am I in' ambient.
WHY CHEAP: consumes the consolidated project_for_cwd helper (quality epic) + optional cheap gix check; MUST be fast (<10ms without --status) since it runs per-prompt — registry read only, no git, in the default mode.
TIMING: after the cwd-consolidation + path-normalization beads (correct inference is the whole feature).
ACCEPTANCE: inside worktree prints repo:tag; outside prints nothing exit 0; default mode does zero git operations (assert); fish integration snippet in README/init.

title: JSON output on all mutating commands (new/fork/done/adopt/rename)
description:
HIGH impact / S effort. Only list/status/repo-list speak JSON today; scripts and agents must scrape human output from exactly the commands they most need to drive. Add --json to new, fork, done, adopt, rename emitting {version:1, action, tag, path, branch, ...} — each command already computes every field before printing.
COORDINATE: land after the status-JSON-schema convergence bead (UX epic) so field names match from day one (tag/path/branch naming per the converged schema).
ACCEPTANCE: each command's --json parses, round-trips through a documented serde struct, and is exercised in the binary E2E suite; human output unchanged without the flag.

title: grove exec: run a command across worktrees in parallel
description:
HIGH impact / M effort. `grove exec [--only a,b] [--frozen|--no-frozen] [--repo X] -- <cmd> [args...]` runs a command in every selected worktree with rayon fan-out, prefixed streaming output ([tag] line...), and a --json exit-code summary. Covers 'cargo test everywhere', 'git fetch everywhere', swarm-wide setup.
WHY CHEAP: rayon fan-out over worktrees exists (git/status.rs scan); --only tag filtering exists in launch.rs; std::process does the rest.
DESIGN NOTES: exit code = 0 iff all succeeded (make the policy explicit); bound parallelism (default min(cores, 8), --jobs N); no shell interpretation — argv passthrough after `--` (document `sh -c` for shell syntax).
ACCEPTANCE: exec over 3 fixtures runs in parallel (timing test), prefixes output per tag, JSON summary lists per-tag exit codes; frozen worktrees skipped by default with reasons.

title: grove prune: classify and batch-remove finished worktrees
description:
HIGH impact / M effort. Scan all projects, classify safe-to-remove (branch merged into base + clean + nothing unpushed) vs kept (with per-project reason), then batch-remove with confirmation, --dry-run, and --yes. Stale worktrees are the #1 entropy source of the workflow; today each needs a manual `grove done`.
WHY CHEAP: done.rs already implements the per-project safety checks; prune = those checks mapped over the registry + a gix merge-base containment test; classify-then-act mirrors the list status scan.
HARD DEPENDENCY: the done safety-policy beads (data-safety epic) define what 'safe' means — build prune ON the fixed policy, sharing one safety-evaluation function with done (do not fork the logic).
ACCEPTANCE: --dry-run prints classification table with reasons and touches nothing; removal path reuses done's code path (single implementation); merged+clean fixture pruned, unmerged/dirty/frozen kept with stated reasons.

title: Lifecycle hooks: post_create / pre_remove commands in per-repo config
description:
HIGH impact / M effort. Per-repo config gains optional hook commands run after new/fork/adopt (post_create) and before done (pre_remove): copy .env, direnv allow, seed .mcp.json, warm caches. Every git-worktree UX layer eventually grows this; fresh worktrees being unusable until hand-setup is the classic gap.
WHY CHEAP: PerRepoConfig + the global/per-repo merge in config/mod.rs make it a two-field schema addition; LaunchOverride.shell_command proves the configured-command pattern exists.
DESIGN NOTES: run with cwd=<worktree>, env GROVE_TAG/GROVE_PATH/GROVE_BRANCH/GROVE_REPO; post_create failure = warn (worktree stays), pre_remove failure = abort done (unless --force); document security posture (config is user-owned, same trust as direnv).
ACCEPTANCE: hooks fire with correct env/cwd on fixtures; failures behave per policy; hooks absent = zero behavior change; config round-trip test.

title: grove doctor: registry/filesystem/git consistency check with --fix
description:
HIGH impact / M effort. Cross-check repos.json, each registry.json, the filesystem, and `git worktree list` for drift: registered paths that no longer exist (suggest done --force / prune), live worktrees missing from the registry (suggest adopt), branch mismatches (registry branch vs checked-out), prunable git metadata, config schema problems, duplicate path identities. Report with actionable hints; --fix applies the safe subset (registry entry removal for vanished dirs, git worktree prune).
WHY CHEAP: all four data sources are already loaded by existing code (GlobalConfig, Registry, GixBackend listing); the review itself found the exact drift classes doctor should detect (vanished dirs, dual identities from unnormalized paths, adopt --move-dir orphans).
ACCEPTANCE: fixture with each drift class → detected with hint; --fix resolves the safe ones and reports the rest; clean setup → 'no issues'; exit code reflects findings (0 clean / 1 issues) for scripting.

title: list: staleness signals (age column, merged marker, --stale/--merged filters)
description:
MEDIUM impact / S effort. Add a last-activity age column (from HEAD commit time, humanized: 3d/2w) and a merged-into-base marker to grove list, with --stale <days> and --merged filters. Turns list into the tool that answers 'which of these 15 worktrees can I kill?' and feeds prune's UX.
WHY CHEAP: StatusDetail already computes last_commit_time (git/status.rs) — it just isn't surfaced in table/JSON; the comfy-table renderer + summary footer just landed, so this is a column, not a redesign. Merged check shares the containment test with prune/done (one implementation).
ACCEPTANCE: age renders in table + JSON (raw timestamp in JSON, humanized in table); --stale 7 filters correctly on fixtures with backdated commits; summary footer counts stale/merged.

title: grove init <shell>: emit gr wrapper + completions; dynamic tag completion
description:
MEDIUM impact / S effort. `grove init fish|bash|zsh` emits everything shell integration needs in one eval-able stream: the gr cd-wrapper function (README currently tells users to hand-write it), static completions, and a dynamic tag-completion hook backed by a hidden `grove __tags` subcommand (fast registry dump, one tag per line). Standard pattern (zoxide/starship init).
WHY CHEAP: clap_complete + hidden __completions exist; __tags is a few lines over the already-loaded registry; registry load is sub-ms JSON.
ACCEPTANCE: `grove init fish | source` in a fresh fish gives working gr + tab-completion of live tags; __tags output is stable/sorted; README updated to the one-liner.

title: Interactive fuzzy picker for cd/done/status when no tag given (TTY only)
description:
MEDIUM impact / S-M effort. `grove cd` with no tag (or --pick) on a TTY presents a fuzzy-searchable selector over tags (repo-grouped), prints the chosen path. Complements strsim did-you-mean with forward selection as tag counts grow. Non-TTY: current behavior (error/inference) unchanged — never block a pipe waiting for input.
DEPENDENCY DECISION: needs a picker dep (e.g. dialoguer/inquire) — check the ≤30-dep budget in AGENTS.md and record the decision; if over budget, defer or feature-gate.
ACCEPTANCE: TTY-gated (is-terminal already in tree); ESC/ctrl-c exits nonzero with no output on stdout; picker output composes with the gr wrapper.

title: Security & path hardening: tag validation, injection, path identity
description: Hardening batch from the security + cross-platform lenses: validate_tag is far too permissive (accepts .., backslash, ';', leading '-'); adopt skips validation entirely (path traversal + merge-overwrite via --mv); wt.exe treats ';' as a command separator (command injection via tag on launch); git argv lacks '--' separators before semi-untrusted refs; non-UTF-8 paths silently become "" in destructive git commands; cwd-vs-registry path matching never normalizes (symlinks, /mnt/c vs /c, NTFS case), so tag inference silently misses and worktrees can exist under two identities.

title: validate_tag: allowlist charset; call it from adopt (path traversal)
description:
PROBLEM (2 lenses): validate_tag (src/cli/new.rs:83-97) only rejects '/', whitespace, and length>40. It accepts '.', '..', backslash (a path separator on Windows/WSL — the primary platform), leading '-', ';' (feeds the wt.exe injection bead), NTFS-invalid chars (: * ? " < > |), Windows reserved device names (CON, NUL, COM1...), and trailing dots/spaces. Tags become directory names via work_dir.join(tag) (new.rs:42, fork.rs:49, rename.rs:43) — `grove new ..\\..\\evil` creates (and grove done later force-removes) a directory OUTSIDE the grove root. WORSE: `grove adopt` never calls validate_tag at all (src/cli/adopt.rs:17-43) — a tag like '../../foo' flows into work_dir.join and, with --mv, move_dir relocates the worktree to an arbitrary filesystem location and persists the traversal tag as a registry key.

FIX: Rewrite validate_tag as an allowlist: chars [A-Za-z0-9._-], first char alphanumeric (not '-' or '.'), reject '.'/'..' outright, reject case-insensitive Windows reserved names, keep the 40-char cap. Call it at the top of adopt::run(). new/fork/rename already route through it, so one fix covers all four.

FILES: src/cli/new.rs, src/cli/adopt.rs.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Table-driven test: '../x', '..', 'a\\b', '-x', 'a;b', 'a:b', 'CON', 'a.', 'a b' all rejected with the reason string; 'feature-1', 'fix.thing', 'a_b' accepted.
- adopt with a traversal tag errors before any filesystem/registry effect.
- Error message tells the user the allowed charset.

title: windows_terminal: escape ';' in wt.exe argv (command injection)
description:
PROBLEM: wt.exe parses an unescaped ';' inside ANY argument as a subcommand separator (post-argv; documented escape is '\\;'). build_argv (src/launch/windows_terminal.rs:31-51) pushes the tab title (= project tag), the converted cwd (= registry project.path), and the command string verbatim. A tag or path containing ';' (currently allowed by validate_tag; needs no quoting so CreateProcess quoting won't protect it) injects an extra wt subcommand: tag 'x;new-tab;calc' → executes an attacker-chosen program on `grove launch`.

FIX: Escape ';' → '\\;' in title, to_windows_path(cwd) result, and command before pushing, per Windows Terminal command-line docs. (Defense in depth: the validate_tag bead also rejects ';' in tags, but paths and configured commands still need escaping here.)

FILES: src/launch/windows_terminal.rs.

ACCEPTANCE: build_argv unit test with title/cwd/command each containing ';' asserts the escaped argv; existing launch snapshot tests updated.

title: shell_backend: '--' separators, ref validation, OsStr-native args
description:
PROBLEM (3 lenses):
1. No '--' end-of-options separator before ref positionals: branch_delete runs ['branch','-D',branch]; remote_branch_delete runs ['push',remote,'--delete',branch]; commit_on_any_remote runs ['branch','-r','--contains',commit] (src/git/shell_backend.rs:63-74, 94, 121-142). Branch values are semi-untrusted (registry.json; adopt harvests from a cloned repo's .git/HEAD). A leading-dash ref is parsed as a git flag — worst case 'git push <remote> --delete --mirror'.
2. run() takes &[&str], forcing target.to_str().unwrap_or_default() at ~5 sites (128,138,158,164,175-176): a non-UTF-8 path silently becomes "" — 'git worktree remove --force ""' — changing the meaning of destructive commands instead of failing.

FIX:
1. Insert "--" before ref positionals where git supports it (branch -D -- <ref>); for push (no '--' support before refspecs) validate with `git check-ref-format --allow-onelevel refs/heads/<branch>` or reject leading-dash; assert commit args are hex OIDs before --contains.
2. Change run() to accept impl AsRef<OsStr> items (Command::arg is OsStr-native); pass Paths directly and delete the lossy conversions. Error messages keep a lossy rendering for display only.

FILES: src/git/shell_backend.rs.

ACCEPTANCE: unit tests — branch named '-D-ish' / '--mirror' is either safely passed as positional or rejected, never parsed as a flag (assert on the constructed argv); worktree ops build argv containing the actual Path (OsStr equality).

title: One path-identity normalization helper for every cwd/registry comparison
description:
PROBLEM: all cwd-vs-registered-path matching uses raw Path::starts_with with no normalization — src/repo/mod.rs:96 (match_work_dir), src/cli/done.rs:33, fork.rs:126, freeze.rs:32, list.rs:374. GROVE_ORIG_CWD comes from the shell and can be a symlinked spelling (~/.claude is a symlink on this machine), /mnt/c/... vs /c/... WSL spelling, or different case on case-insensitive NTFS/drvfs, while registry paths are stored as-written at creation time. Result: tag/repo inference silently misses ('cwd is not inside any known worktree'), and the same worktree can exist under two identities because adopt canonicalizes but new does not. RELATED: std::fs::canonicalize on native Windows returns \\\\?\\C:\\... verbatim paths that get persisted and later break wt.exe --startingDirectory; AGENTS.md's tech-stack canon names dunce for exactly this but dunce is not in Cargo.toml.

FIX:
1. Add paths::normalize_identity(&Path) -> PathBuf: canonicalize via dunce (add the dep — it is already canon in AGENTS.md), apply the existing /mnt/X -> /X WSL normalization, case-fold the drive component for drive-letter paths.
2. Route BOTH sides of every comparison through it: match_work_dir and every resolve-tag-from-cwd site (done/fork/freeze/list). NOTE: the quality epic has a bead consolidating those duplicated loops into RepoContext::project_for_cwd — land that consolidation FIRST or TOGETHER so normalization is applied in one place, not five.
3. Normalize at write time too: grove new stores the same identity adopt does.

FILES: src/paths.rs, src/repo/mod.rs, Cargo.toml (+ call sites via the consolidation bead).

ACCEPTANCE:
- Test: registry path stored as /c/work/x, cwd given as symlink-to-/c/work/x and as /mnt/c/work/x → both resolve the tag.
- Test: new + adopt of equivalent spellings produce one identity.
- No \\\\?\\ prefixes persisted (Windows-targeted unit test on the helper).

title: launch: detect native wezterm; gate WSL->Windows path conversion
description:
PROBLEM (2 findings):
1. autodetect() (src/launch/mod.rs:62-68) probes PATH only for 'wezterm.exe' and 'wt.exe'. On native Linux/macOS the binary is 'wezterm', so users with WezTerm installed get NoTerminalAvailable — even though Wezterm::new() itself probes both names (wezterm.rs:18). Detection is inconsistent with the launcher it feeds.
2. to_windows_path() is applied to the tab cwd UNCONDITIONALLY (wezterm.rs:37). That is only correct for the Windows wezterm build driven from WSL. On native Linux/macOS, any path whose first component is a single letter (/d/projects) is silently rewritten to D:\\projects; a Linux-native wezterm on WSL receives Windows paths it cannot chdir into.

FIX: autodetect probes which("wezterm") too; gate the path conversion on actually running under WSL driving a Windows binary (detect via /proc/version containing 'Microsoft'/'WSL', or an explicit launch config flag), pass paths through untouched otherwise.

FILES: src/launch/mod.rs, src/launch/wezterm.rs, src/paths.rs (WSL detection helper).

ACCEPTANCE: unit tests for autodetect with mocked which results (or injectable probe); build_argv test asserting cwd passes through unconverted when not WSL->Windows; conversion still applied in the WSL case.

title: GROVE_CONFIG_DIR env override; fix literal-tilde fallback
description:
PROBLEM (2 lenses): the config dir is hardwired to directories::BaseDirs (src/main.rs:42-44) with NO env override — grep for GROVE_CONFIG in src/ finds nothing. Consequences: (a) no test can invoke the compiled binary hermetically, which is why zero binary-level tests exist (the tests epic's E2E bead depends on this); (b) agents/scripts cannot point grove at a fixture; (c) main() unconditionally runs migrate::run_if_needed against the real config on every invocation. BONUS BUG: the fallback is PathBuf::from("~/.config/grove") — the tilde is never expanded, so if BaseDirs::new() returns None, grove creates a literal directory named '~' relative to cwd during migration.

FIX: Check GROVE_CONFIG_DIR before BaseDirs; replace the tilde-literal fallback with a hard error ('cannot determine config directory; set GROVE_CONFIG_DIR'). Document the variable in README and --help (top-level long_about).

FILES: src/main.rs, README.md.

ACCEPTANCE: unit test on the resolution order (env wins); running with GROVE_CONFIG_DIR=<tempdir> touches nothing outside it (asserted by the E2E bead that builds on this); no PathBuf::from("~...") remains.

title: Scrub credentials from git stderr in error output
description:
PROBLEM: GroveError::GitCommandFailed embeds full git stderr (src/git/shell_backend.rs:44-47). For fetch/push failures git echoes the remote URL; a remote configured as https://user:token@host leaks the token into terminal output and any logs capturing grove errors.

FIX: scrub userinfo from URL-looking substrings ('://<userinfo>@' → '://***@') before embedding stderr; apply in the one place the error is constructed.

FILES: src/git/shell_backend.rs.

ACCEPTANCE: unit test: stderr containing https://alice:hunter2@example.com renders with ***; normal stderr unchanged.

title: Performance: eliminate redundant scans, opens, and walks in list/status
description: 'Fast' is the product claim and WSL1 (primary platform) has ~10x stat() cost. Review found grove list does two full worktree scans per project plus a second dirwalk for an untracked count the table never displays, opens every repo twice, computes ahead/behind with two boundary walks over shared history, and gix is compiled without its performance features. Fix order matters: these beads mostly touch src/git/status.rs and are serialized.

title: Single status sweep: merge is_dirty + untracked; skip dirwalk when not displayed
description:
PROBLEM (perf lens, HIGH x2): compute() (src/git/status.rs:176-208) does TWO full worktree filesystem sweeps per project: repo.is_dirty() (head-tree-vs-index diff + full index-vs-worktree scan; early-exits only when dirty, so the common CLEAN case pays the full scan) then count_untracked() (a second complete status iteration whose dirwalk re-stats every tracked file and traverses all directories). On WSL1 (~10x stat cost) this roughly doubles the scan-bound portion of `grove list` per clean worktree — 40 worktrees = 40 redundant full-tree scans. Worse: table/--short modes never display untracked (after the untracked-dirty bead they will consume the flag — coordinate!), yet always pay the dirwalk; only --json serializes the count. Same double-scan pattern in collect_dirty_files() (117-159: full iteration then is_dirty() fallback for staged-only).

FIX:
1. One repo.status(Discard).untracked_files(Files) iteration per worktree: count Untracked/DirectoryContents items, set dirty on any other IndexWorktree/TreeIndex item. Keep a cheap staged-changes early-exit. Replaces is_dirty()+count_untracked().
2. Thread a want_untracked (or StatusDepth) parameter from ListArgs: table/short use the early-exit variant, --json pays for the full count. (Table still needs untracked>0 as a BOOLEAN after the untracked-dirty fix — the early-exit variant provides that without a full count.)
3. Fix collect_dirty_files to handle TreeIndex items in its main loop instead of the trailing is_dirty().

FILES: src/git/status.rs, src/cli/list.rs.

PREREQ: land the untracked-counts-as-dirty bug fix first (same files; it defines the semantics this bead optimizes).

ACCEPTANCE: existing status fixtures pass; new test asserts clean-repo compute performs one traversal (observable via a counting mock or by asserting the new API shape); `grove list` JSON still reports exact untracked counts.

title: Open each repo once per list/status; drop eager head_id
description:
PROBLEM: every worktree is opened TWICE per `grove list`: GixBackend::open() (src/git/gix_backend.rs:45-53) runs ThreadSafeRepository::open (git-dir discovery, config parsing, ref-db setup), builds a Worktree, discards the repo; compute() (status.rs:177) immediately re-runs ThreadSafeRepository::open on the same path. GixBackend::open also eagerly resolves head_id() (ref resolution + peel) though the list path only reads wt.branch(). Same double-open in compute_detail via cli/status.rs:49-50. Net: N extra repo opens + N unused HEAD peels per invocation — several config-file reads each on WSL1.

FIX: Make Worktree carry the opened ThreadSafeRepository (or change compute/compute_detail to accept &gix::Repository / the ThreadSafeRepository), and compute head_oid lazily only for callers that need it (done's safety check does; list does not).

FILES: src/git/gix_backend.rs, src/git/status.rs, src/cli/list.rs, src/cli/status.rs.

ACCEPTANCE: no ThreadSafeRepository::open call remains in compute/compute_detail (they receive the handle); all status/list/done tests pass; done still gets a HEAD oid where it needs one.

title: Enable gix performance features (zlib-ng, parallel)
description:
PROBLEM: gix is built with default-features=false and NO performance features (Cargo.toml:33) — object inflation falls back to pure-Rust flate2 (no zlib-ng) and gix-internal parallelism is disabled. Compile-flag-only speedup, commonly 20-40% on object-decode-heavy paths (the ahead/behind rev walks), left on the table in a tool whose description says 'Fast'.

FIX: add "max-performance-safe" (or minimally "zlib-ng" + "parallel") to the gix feature list. No code changes. Verify build on WSL1 (zlib-ng needs cmake/cc — if the build environment rejects it, fall back to "zlib-stock" + "parallel" and note why in Cargo.toml comment).

FILES: Cargo.toml.

ACCEPTANCE: cargo build + full test suite green; rough before/after timing of `grove list` on the dev machine recorded in the bead comments on close.

title: Single left-right walk for ahead/behind; dedupe upstream code; handle remote '.'
description:
PROBLEM (perf + correctness lenses):
1. Ahead/behind is computed with two independent boundary rev walks (local hiding upstream, then upstream hiding local) — each re-decodes the shared history around the merge base, roughly doubling commit-decode work per project (src/git/status.rs:103-112, 249-258).
2. The ~40-line upstream-resolution + walk block is duplicated verbatim between upstream_info() (66-115) and compute_ahead_behind() (211-261) — any fix must land twice.
3. CORRECTNESS: upstream resolution assumes branch.<name>.remote names a real remote and rewrites merge_ref to refs/remotes/<remote>/<branch>. When remote is '.' (local tracking branch: git branch --track feat main) the constructed ref refs/remotes/./main never resolves → ahead/behind silently None → branch renders clean/unknown.

FIX: one fn upstream_status(repo, branch) -> Result<Option<UpstreamStatus{label, ahead, behind}>> consumed by both compute() and compute_detail(); count both directions in a single symmetric-difference walk (rev-list --left-right --count algorithm: walk from both tips, tag each commit with its side, stop at merge base); special-case remote == "." to compare against refs/heads/<upstream_branch>.

FILES: src/git/status.rs.

ACCEPTANCE: fixture with local tracking branch ('.') reports correct ahead/behind; existing ahead/behind fixtures unchanged; the duplicated block is gone (single definition).

title: Parallelize multi-tag status; stop re-reading context registry; fold exists() into scan
description:
Three LOW perf findings, one bead:
1. `grove status a b c` computes each StatusDetail sequentially (src/main.rs:229-238) — each is a repo open + full scan + rev walks. Compute via rayon par_iter, print in order.
2. load_repo_rows() (src/cli/list.rs:385-400) re-reads and re-parses registry.json for the context repo whose Registry was already loaded into cx.registry by discover(). Reuse cx.registry for cx.id.
3. The per-project project.path.exists() stat loop runs serially BEFORE the parallel status scan; fold the missing-check into the parallel scan (open failure already yields status None — derive `missing` there).

FILES: src/main.rs, src/cli/list.rs.

ACCEPTANCE: multi-tag status output order deterministic (matches arg order); list output identical on fixtures; no Registry::load call for cx.id in list.

title: Code quality: dedupe helpers, error boundaries, dead code
description: Maintainability debt found by the quality lens: jaro-winkler 'did you mean' implemented 5x with drifting thresholds; cwd-inference loop copy-pasted 6x; registry mutate-save ritual 6x; upstream_info/compute_ahead_behind ~45 identical lines; ~400 lines of duplicated test fixtures; anyhow/thiserror boundary inverted in git/status.rs (done.rs fabricates 'git command failed: git status' for in-process gix errors); dead code kept alive by allow-attributes.

title: Consolidate cwd inference: RepoContext::project_for_cwd + repo::orig_cwd
description:
PROBLEM: the `GROVE_ORIG_CWD || current_dir()` idiom appears 6+ times, and the longest-prefix 'which registered project contains cwd' loop is copy-pasted verbatim in done.rs:17-45 (resolve_tag), fork.rs:114-137 (infer_source_from_cwd), freeze.rs:19-42 (resolve_tag) — done's own doc comment admits 'mirroring grove freeze / grove fork'. list.rs:366-382 (cwd_repo_id) re-implements repo/mod.rs match_work_dir at repo granularity. Any path-normalization fix currently needs 4-5 edits (and the hardening epic's normalization bead needs exactly this consolidation as its landing site).

FIX: add repo::orig_cwd() -> Option<PathBuf> and RepoContext::project_for_cwd(&self) -> Option<&str>; replace the three project-level loops and list.rs's private repo-level clone (call match_work_dir). The status-cwd-inference bead in the UX epic consumes the same helper.

FILES: src/repo/mod.rs, src/cli/done.rs, src/cli/fork.rs, src/cli/freeze.rs, src/cli/list.rs (net deletion).

ACCEPTANCE: one implementation of each concern (grep); all existing inference tests pass against the shared helper; done/freeze/fork error texts preserved.

title: RepoContext::update_registry helper; RegistryError as transparent GroveError
description:
PROBLEM: the registry mutate-and-persist ritual — clone cx.registry, mutate, .map_err(|e| GroveError::Registry{msg: e.to_string()}), save — is copy-pasted in 6 commands (new.rs:61-67, fork.rs:73-79, adopt.rs:62-68, rename.rs:34-78 with TWO divergent save sites, freeze.rs:60-64, done.rs:103-109; 18 occurrences of that map_err closure), flattening the structured RegistryError to a string every time and cloning the full Registry per invocation.

FIX: RepoContext::update_registry(&self, f: impl FnOnce(&mut Registry) -> Result<T, RegistryError>) -> Result<T, GroveError>, plus #[error(transparent)] Registry(#[from] RegistryError) on GroveError (kill the stringly Registry{msg} variant). NOTE: the data-safety epic's locking bead wants all mutation through ONE code path — implement the lock inside this helper; coordinate the two beads (this one can land the helper, that one adds the lock, either order but same seam).

FILES: src/repo/mod.rs, src/error.rs, the six command modules (mechanical).

ACCEPTANCE: zero .map_err Registry{msg} closures remain; rename has one save path; error output preserves RegistryError detail.

title: Remove or wire dead code: WorktreeManager::list, compute_all, terminal field, use_color alias
description:
